repair.content:
Use degree tH-tN. Take positive HN subobject and zero-slope quotient; reduce one filtration step on positive part. Each quotient degree falls at most1 and stays>=0. Iterate total integral degree to0. Largest positive step preserves Lemma5.4 endpoints; existing period-Hom argument then applies.

By Theorem3.12 and BC full embedding, HomVS(Vst^r,Bk)=Hom_R(t^rL,Bk). Restriction from L0 has elementary divisors t^a,0<=a<=r; kernel/cokernel killed t^r. k0 zero,r0 iso.

Require both factors in the interval; nonnegative extension closure used elsewhere is valid.

Reverse final inequality; correct multiplicity and insert corresponding multiplicity in Hom formula.

Use i1 if p notdiv k; p^r if k=p^r*m,m>1; p^(r-1) if pure power. Binomial valuations0,0,1. Correct b_(i,k-1) to b_(i,k-i).

Keep Hom=W; change Ext1 to0 as already proved and used in(ii).

Use M*{r}, and M_K* for j<=0. Remark9.2 already preserves the twist.

Use Bst+ in positive-target kernel or full BdR target; take admissible N subset L and t^rV subset Vst^r. For5.18 choose N subset t^-rL0; do not require L0 subset N.

Replace the final sum by difference, or change one sign in first map.

Use finite type. Diagram surjectivity uses upper exactness and de Rham identifications, not finite length.

Use perfectness of proper-factor RΓ(Y,Zp); bounded finite-projective resolution commutes with RΓ(T,-) and gives projection formula.
